verdict_text: YES. The script casts exactly the 112 listed projection matrices to bfloat16 via `tensor.float().to(torch.bfloat16)` (a no-op float32 pass-through since inputs are already float32, satisfying round-to-nearest-even semantics), leaves all other 2 tensors (`embed_tokens.weight`, `lm_head.weight`) as float32 unchanged, drops nothing (the buffer regex is an intentional never-matching pattern, consistent with "no buffers to delete"), preserves all 114 names, and asserts the four required checks before writing. The sharding function correctly packs by cumulative tensor-data size against the 268,435,456-byte cap and isolates oversized tensors (the two 412 MB embedding/lm_head tensors) alone in their own shard, producing a valid `weight_map` and index file.
